preregistered_hypothesis: With solver.saveat=86400 s, successive BMI.update_until calls at 6-hour endpoints would make those endpoints effective UserDemand management boundaries and reproduce the 6-hour DUMMY-19G trajectory.

observations.failure: applied root allocation after BMI call 2 differs from frozen 6-hour reference

pinned_source_reconciliation.bmi_tstop_insertion: core/src/bmi.jl::BMI.update_until adds the requested endpoint to allocation.time.tstops.
pinned_source_reconciliation.allocation_solve: core/src/model.jl::loopheader! calls update_allocation! at allocation tstops.
pinned_source_reconciliation.record_flag: The call uses record=is_saveat_time(t, allocation.time). For a 6-hour BMI boundary with daily saveat this is false.
pinned_source_reconciliation.user_demand_state_write: parse_allocations! is where UserDemand.allocated and UserDemand.inflow_link_allocated are populated from the optimized LP flows.
pinned_source_reconciliation.physical_use: The physical UserDemand flow formulation consumes these stored applied allocation values.
pinned_source_reconciliation.consequence: A sub-saveat BMI tstop can solve the LP without committing the new UserDemand allocation to the physical UserDemand state.

scientific_effect: BMI.update_until can add allocation solve boundaries, but in the pinned implementation a non-saveat allocation solve is not sufficient to update the UserDemand allocation state used by physical realization. Therefore a coupler cannot obtain a finer effective UserDemand management clock merely by calling BMI.update_until more frequently than saveat.
